summary.intent: Investigate and fix a cross-platform E2E CI failure (`FATAL: Cannot test sync without successful edit.`) that appeared after merging the phase 46 PR, then resolve CodeRabbit review comments on the phase 47 PR and audit all mutative web paths for correct SDK client routing.
summary.outcome: Fixed the E2E failure (PR #495, merged) by updating the stale `edit-filepointer.mjs` test helper to match the `updateFileMetadata` contract changed in #488; resolved all CodeRabbit findings on PR #494 including a `deleteFileVersion` pin leak, a `restoreFileVersion` pin leak, two missing `cas.ts` test cases, and removal of dead-code upload handlers that bypassed the SDK client; captured a follow-up todo for `useSharedWriteOps`; marked 10 phase-46/47 todos complete; and confirmed the phase 46 Linux UAT.

repo: `ci-e2e.yml` has no `pull_request` trigger — Desktop E2E only runs on push to main or manual dispatch, so SDK contract breaks can reach main undetected.

The `desktop` path filter in `ci-e2e.yml` includes `packages/crypto/src/**` but not `packages/sdk-core/**` or `tests/desktop-e2e/**`, meaning SDK changes never auto-trigger Desktop E2E even on push to main.
`.mjs` E2E helper scripts (`packages/sdk-core/scripts/`) are not type-checked or linted — they can silently drift from SDK contract changes and only fail at runtime in CI.
`useSharedWriteOps.ts` uses `SharedWriteContext` and local refs (not the SDK client's `folderTree`) by design — shared-with-me folders are a separate subsystem not tracked by the owner's folderTree.
`handleAddFile`/`handleAddFiles` in `useFileOperations.ts` were dead code — the live upload path runs through `useDropUpload.ts` → `getSdkClient().uploadFiles()`.
NestJS ValidationPipe runs with `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` and `@IsNotEmpty` on IPNS publish DTOs — empty/undefined fields produce a fast (0.5s) deterministic 400, not a timeout.
`replaceFileInFolder` is still used by the version-restore path but NOT by the normal edit path post-#488; only `restoreVersion` returns an `ipnsRecord`.
GSD commit helper has known false-negatives in this repo; git is used directly for GSD-adjacent commits on this branch.

code.finding: Contract changed in #488: `updateFileMetadata` now publishes the file IPNS record internally and returns `{ ipnsName, metadataCid, newSequenceNumber, prunedCids }`. It no longer returns `ipnsRecord`. The old return shape `{ ipnsRecord, prunedCids }` is documented as replaced in the built `.d.ts`.

Was destructuring `{ ipnsRecord }` from `updateFileMetadata` (now undefined post-#488) and passing it to `replaceFileInFolder`, producing a batch-publish entry with undefined `ipnsName`/`record`/`metadataCid` → deterministic 400 on all three E2E platforms.

`deleteFileVersion` bare-awaited `updateFileMetadata` and discarded `prunedCids`, unlike sibling methods `replaceFile` (line 1224) and `restoreFileVersion` (line 1313) which both capture and return them. On a 409-conflict merge round, this caused orphaned pins.

`handleRestoreVersion` ignored the SDK-returned `prunedCids` (conflict-merge pruning) and only unpinned web-computed cap-prune CIDs from `computeRestoreVersionUpdate`. Same latent conflict-merge pin leak as `deleteFileVersion`.
Jitter formula `base * (0.5 + Math.random() * 0.5)` spans only [0.5x, 1.0x) — one-sided, biased early. Line 20 documents '±50% jitter' implying [0.5x, 1.5x). Fixed to `base * (0.5 + Math.random())`.

`handleAddFile` (line 44–175) and `handleAddFiles` (line 187–334) were dead code using old direct `sdk-core` `addFileToFolder`/`addFilesToFolder` calls that bypass the SDK client's `folderTree`. No component consumed them; removed.

workflow: When CI log artifacts are expired or too large for `gh run view --log`, use `gh api /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs` to fetch raw step logs.
1Password SSH signing agent can get wedged after a timed-out commit attempt — subsequent commits return `failed to fill whole buffer`. Requires quitting and relaunching 1Password to recover.
Background unsandboxed commits (`dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`, `run_in_background: true`) are the reliable pattern for SSH-signed commits with 1Password in this environment.
Use `git mv` (not `mv`) when moving GSD todos from `pending/` to `completed/` to preserve git history.
`gh workflow run` manual dispatch forces all path-filter-gated E2E jobs on — the only way to validate a fix on a branch when the path filter doesn't include the changed file.

When a CodeRabbit test finding references a second `publishWithCas` call inside a try/catch for error-property assertions, restructure to a single invocation with `expect(...).rejects` — mock bleed from redundant invocations creates confusing assertion failures.

friction: 1Password SSH signing agent wedged after timed-out commit attempts — required app restart and multiple retry cycles across the session.
Transient `could not write index` git error from lint-staged aborted a commit; edits survived staged but required diagnosis and retry.
CI log artifacts were unavailable via `gh run view --log` (expired/too large); had to fall back to raw GitHub API job log endpoint.

`ci-e2e.yml` has no `pull_request` trigger and the `desktop` path filter excludes `packages/sdk-core/**` — the #488 contract break was never caught before reaching main, and the fix PR (#495) couldn't auto-validate either.
GSD commit helper (`gsd_run query commit`) has known false-negatives in this environment; had to use git directly for GSD-related commits.
open_items: Add `packages/sdk-core/src/**`, `packages/sdk/src/**`, and `tests/desktop-e2e/**` to the `desktop` path filter in `.github/workflows/ci-e2e.yml`, and consider adding a `pull_request` trigger so SDK contract changes are caught before reaching main.

Route `useSharedWriteOps` mutations through the SDK client for single folder-state ownership on shared folders — captured as todo `.planning/todos/pending/2026-06-15-route-shared-folder-writes-through-the-sdk-client.md` (area: `shares`, medium scope, multi-PR).

The `useSharedWriteOps` shared-folder write path (`uploadToSharedFolder`, `createSharedSubfolder`, `renameInSharedFolder`, `deleteFromSharedFolder`, `updateSharedFile`) still uses direct `SharedWriteContext` refs rather than the SDK client's `folderTree` — by design today but flagged for future unification.
